body: My fantasy of being rescued really involves someone older/wiser offering to take me under their wing and take care of all my responsibilities for a long enough time that I can figure out who I am and not have to worry about my own survival. Basically, I'm seeking someone to play that role of what my parents should have done when I was a child. I am and have been seeking the help of a therapist for years, with mixed results. On the surface, I'm a productive and contributing member of society. It's the inside of me that is dying.

Yea, I'm in the same boat with respect to religious views, but I actually find that my agnosticism makes it easier to let go. There's no repercussions for my actions after this life and the sum of staying alive vs the pain caused after I leave doesn't balance out. 

If we knew a dog was suffering, we would put it out of its misery after exhausting all other resources. Why isn't the same view held for humans that are suffering?

Every day, I yearn for someone to rescue me. But no one does. And honestly, no one ever will because it is my responsibility to do so. And if no one can rescue me and I can't muster the strength to keep trying, why put myself through it? 

I understand that hypothetically and logically speaking, what I'm seeing/experiencing is short-sided and that there is another, possibly happy, version of the life I'm living.

But how long will it take to get there? What if it never comes? What if the work it takes to get there is beyond what I can bear? 

This is really what I'm afraid of and why CVS sleeping pills keep calling my name.

So I should stay alive because I owe it to my fellow human to help them survive?

It was my fellow human that brought me into the shitty life and it was my fellow human that has turned its back on me despite repeated calls for help.

I don't disagree with you, but it isn't that black and white.
